topic: VFR flight planning and VMC minima (SS05)
summary: Good VFR planning covers weather, NOTAMs, fuel, weight, route and airspace, then keeps checking in flight. Legal fuel reserves for Part-21 aeroplanes are 10 minutes in sight of an aerodrome by day, 30 minutes by day otherwise and 45 minutes at night. Know the VMC minima and the FREDA checks, and keep 'Take 2' (2 NM or 200 ft) from controlled airspace. Built from CAA Safety Sense Leaflet 5.
src: Safety Sense Leaflet 5: Flight under VFR
sections: Pre-flight planning
Use threat and error management: spot the threats, then plan how to handle them
Brief weather for departure, route, destination and alternates. Avoid en-route flight below 1,500 ft AGL
Get NOTAMs and check airspace and temporary restrictions
Check weight and balance and performance for the actual load and runway
Carry a paper chart as backup. A Maximum Elevation Figure leaves no margin by itself
Fuel reserves
Part-21 aeroplanes: 10 minutes by day in sight of the aerodrome, 30 minutes by day otherwise, 45 minutes by night
Helicopters: 20 minutes
These are minima: plan to land with more
VMC minima in the UK
At or above 10,000 ft (FL100): 8 km visibility, 1,500 m horizontal and 1,000 ft vertical from cloud
Below 10,000 ft and above 3,000 ft amsl or 1,000 ft above terrain: 5 km, same cloud distances
At or below 3,000 ft amsl, Classes A to E: 5 km with the same cloud distances
Class F or G at or below 3,000 ft: 5 km, clear of cloud and the surface in sight
UK reduction for Class F or G at or below 140 kt IAS by day with the surface in sight: 1,500 m visibility
UK Class D exemption at or below 3,000 ft amsl by day at 140 kt IAS or less, clear of cloud, surface in sight
In-flight monitoring
About 80% of your time should be spent looking outside
Do FREDA checks about every 10 minutes: Fuel, Radio, Engine, Direction, Altimeter
The regional pressure setting often reads low, so allow for it
Know your ATS: Basic Service versus Traffic Service
Use Take 2: keep 2 NM or 200 ft clear of controlled airspace edges
Arrival and review
Call the destination about 10 minutes before arrival and plan an overhead join where appropriate
Review the flight afterwards: what went well and what to improve

quiz.why: 45 minutes at night for Part-21 aeroplanes.

quiz.q: VMC visibility at FL100 and above:

o: Keep 2 NM or 200 ft from controlled airspace
Make two radio calls before entering any ATZ
Fly two turns of a hold before joining
Carry two minutes of extra fuel per leg
quiz.why: A margin of 2 NM or 200 ft helps avoid infringements.

quiz.q: About how much of your time should you spend looking outside?
quiz.why: Roughly 80% of the time outside, 20% inside.
